name: Microlibrary Taman Bima
view: long elevation: the raised reading box (concrete floor and roof slabs on a steel frame) with its grid of ice-cream-bucket openings, over the open stage
note: No photo on Commons. The bucket grid is shown at reduced density (about 2,000 buckets in reality) and without the binary open/closed pattern; overall length-to-height ratio and column spacing are approximate (no dimensions published beyond 160 m2). The full-length stair is left out because its position in this view is not confirmed.

name: Monterrey Housing
view: street elevation of a three-storey row: ground-floor houses below, two-storey duplexes above alternating with empty double-height bays (drawn as recesses) under one continuous roof
note: No photo on Commons. Bay count, window positions and sizes are schematic; the defining idea (built bays alternating with roofed voids for residents to fill) is from the sources.

name: Nueva Esperanza School
note: No photo on Commons. Sources confirm a small (36 m2) one-room school: timber platform on piles, hexagonal boat-like base, cane walls and a woven palm-thatch roof, but not the roof shape or wall heights, so an elevation would be guessed.

name: Nur Alem
view: front elevation: the 80 m glass sphere resting on its low plinth building, floor levels shown as latitude lines
note: Kazakhstan has no freedom of panorama for buildings; several Expo 2017 pavilion photos have been deleted from Commons. The only survivors are File:Storm over Astana 1.jpg / 2.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, 1920x1080), lightning shots where the sphere is not the clear subject, so drawn instead. Proportions from sources: 80 m diameter, 100 m total height, sphere set on a plinth building; plinth width is approximate.

name: Oberrealta Chapel
note: Category has ten more exterior photos (series 1-10 von 10).

name: Palmyra House
view: long elevation of one of the two oblong timber volumes: two storeys behind framed panels of horizontal palmyra-trunk louvres, thin roof edge, on a low plinth
note: No photo on Commons. Shows only one of the two offset volumes (an elevation cannot separate them). Panel count and length-to-height ratio are approximate; roofs are low standing-seam aluminium, drawn as a thin edge.

name: Park Vijversburg Visitor Centre
note: No photo of the pavilion on Commons (Category:Park Vijversburg holds only park art and historic views). The building is co-designed with Studio Maks (Marieke Kums). Its defining idea is in plan: three curving glass corridors radiating from a sunken triangular hall, the glass carrying a thin gravel roof. A trial elevation read as a fence of columns, which is misleading, and the wing angles needed for an axonometric are not published, so not drawn.

name: Parliament Library Building
note: Only free photo is File:Parliament library.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, category Buildings by Raj Rewal) at 660x467, below the 1200px floor; worth using if the owner relaxes the size rule. Not drawn: sources confirm a low red-sandstone mandala plan with twelve domes of different sizes and structures (fibre cement, steel lattice, glass), but not how they line up in any elevation, so a drawing would be guesswork.

name: Paulistano Athletic Club Gymnasium
note: No photo on Commons (Category:Club Athlético Paulistano has only a 457px aerial). Sources agree on a rectangular podium, six concrete blades in a circle carrying a concrete ring, and a central metal roof hung from it by twelve steel cables, but not on the blade and cable geometry seen in elevation (whether blades rise above the ring, where the cables anchor). Too uncertain to draw.

name: Pearling Path Visitor Centre
note: No photo on Commons. Sources describe a perforated concrete roof plane on a forest of columns over the ruins of an amara, a perimeter wall and triangular wind towers, but give no heights, column count or opening shapes; an elevation would be guesswork.
